gemini-2.5-flash.exact_reserve_text: During 2022 the Syndicate released $85.9m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2021: $105.2m), arising predominantly from the Political Risk & Violence, Marine and Property divisions (2021: predominantly from the Treaty, Marine and Energy divisions). These releases were due to favourable claims development on prior year losses during 2022.

named_events.loss_description: The Syndicate has material exposure to claims arising from the Russia and Ukraine crisis that arose when Russia invaded Ukraine towards the end of February 2022. The claims could come from issues more directly linked to Russia's invasion for example factories hit by Russian troops or from the new sanctions imposed on Russia by other countries. The current estimated ultimate claims are $259.8m gross and $106.9m net of reinsurance. After inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this increases to $126.6m.

The Syndicate has exposure to a number of natural catastrophe events that occurred in 2022. The largest of these is Hurricane Ian. The current estimated ultimate claims for these events are $100.7m gross and $64.1m net of reinsurance. After inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to $57.5m.

named_events.loss_description: The Syndicate has exposure to losses emanating from the Covid-19 pandemic and the ensuing Global Economic Crisis. After inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to $112.0m (2021: $132.0m).

named_events.loss_description: The Syndicate has exposure to a number of natural catastrophe events that occurred in 2021. The largest of these is Hurricane Ida and US Winter Storms. The Syndicate also has exposure to a number of non-elemental catastrophe events that occurred in 2021. The largest of these is South Africa Riots. After inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this increases to $33.8m (2021: $39.2m).

gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: In 2022, Syndicate 1084 reported a reserve release of $85.9 million for prior years, representing a 2.97% reduction of its opening gross claims outstanding. This favourable development primarily stemmed from the Political Risk & Violence, Marine, and Property divisions. The syndicate also reported significant ultimate claims exposures for 2022 events such as the Russia and Ukraine crisis ($106.9m net) and Hurricane Ian ($64.1m net), as well as for prior year events including the COVID-19 pandemic and Global Economic Crisis ($112.7m net ultimate claims), Hurricane Ida and US Winter Storms ($78.7m net ultimate claims), and South Africa Riots ($32.3m net ultimate claims). Other named catastrophe events in 2022 included flood losses in Australia and South Africa, and in 2021, European Floods following storm Bernd.
